DC Power Flow Architecture Design

Executive Summary

Recommendation: DC should be a FormulationTrait, not a separate problem type.

This recommendation maximizes code reuse, maintains architectural consistency, and requires minimal implementation changes. DC power flow fits naturally into the existing formulation system as a third option alongside PowerInjection and CurrentInjection.

1. Design Rationale

1.1 Why FormulationTrait (Recommended)

Key Insight: DC power flow is fundamentally a different mathematical representation of the same physical system, not a different problem class.

AspectPowerInjectionCurrentInjectionDCPowerFlow (proposed)
Variablesθ, V (polar)Vr, Vi (rectangular)θ only
EquationsP=0, Q=0 (nonlinear)Ir=0, Ii=0 (nonlinear)P=0 (linear)
PhysicsFull ACFull ACLinearized approximations
SystemSame buses, branches, loadsSame buses, branches, loadsSame buses, branches, loads

Architectural Alignment:

# Current design philosophy (from CLAUDE.md):
# "Formulations determine the mathematical representation of network equations"
# - What equations are solved (residuals)
# - What variables are used
# - How kernels compute contributions

# DC fits PERFECTLY:
struct DCPowerFlow <: FormulationTrait end

# Variables: Only angles (no voltage magnitudes)
# Residuals: Only active power balance (no reactive power)
# Kernels: Linear approximations (P = B'θ)

Benefits:

  1. Maximum code reuse: SystemModel, AddressManager, model registry, topology detection, reporting - all work unchanged
  2. Consistent API: Same problem → solve workflow as AC formulations
  3. Natural extension: Models already support formulation-specific variables/residuals via vars_by_formulation dict
  4. Type safety: Compiler prevents mixing incompatible formulations
  5. Minimal changes: Add 1 trait + formulation-specific metadata for each model

1.2 Why NOT Separate Problem Type

A separate DCPowerFlowProblem would create architectural friction:

Problems:

  1. Duplicated infrastructure: Need separate workspace types, solution types, solver paths
  2. API divergence: Users would need to learn different patterns for AC vs DC
  3. Code duplication: Linear algebra code would be reimplemented (but simpler)
  4. Maintenance burden: Changes to address management, reporting, etc. must be applied to both paths
  5. Lost opportunities: Can't easily compare AC vs DC convergence on same system

When separate problem types ARE appropriate:

  • OPF (optimization problem, not just equations): Different objective functions, constraints
  • Dynamic simulation: Has state variables (x, f) in addition to algebraic (y, g)
  • Transient stability: Time-domain integration, different solver algorithms

DC power flow shares the same problem structure as AC (solve g(y)=0), just with different g and y.

Changes needed:

# Each model adds DC formulation metadata
function model_metadata(::Type{Bus})
    metadata = ModelMetadata(...)
    
    # DC formulation: only angles, only P residuals
    metadata.vars_by_formulation[DCPowerFlow] = [
        ModelVar(:theta, AlgebVar(), Internal(); description="Voltage angle", units="rad")
    ]
    
    metadata.residuals_by_formulation[DCPowerFlow] = [
        ModelResidual(:p, AlgebRes(), SharedRes(), :Bus, :p, :key; description="Active power balance")
    ]
    
    return metadata
end

# New kernel for DC residual calculation
function calc_residuals!(ws::ResidualBuffers, model::BranchVec, _external::NamedTuple, ::DCPowerFlow)
    # Linear: P_ij = (theta_i - theta_j) / x
    dc_branch_kernel!(ws.res_vals.p_i, ws.res_vals.p_j,
                      ws.var_vals.theta_i, ws.var_vals.theta_j,
                      model.x, ws.active_mask)
end

2.5 DAE Layer (100% reuse)

  • DAE struct (y, g vectors) ✓
  • ResidualBuffers workspace ✓
  • ADCache autodiff wrapper ✓
  • Gather/scatter operations ✓

Why: DC just has smaller y and g vectors (only angles, only P).

2.6 Problem API (100% reuse with dispatch)

  • ACPowerFlowProblem{F<:FormulationTrait} ✓
  • solve(prob, alg) interface ✓
  • PowerFlowSolution struct ✓
  • Algorithm presets (NewtonRaphson, RobustNewton) ✓

Why: Generic over formulation type parameter F.

2.7 Topology (100% reuse)

  • split_islands() ✓
  • MultiIslandSolution ✓
  • Connected component analysis ✓

Why: Topology is independent of formulation.

2.8 Reporting (100% reuse)

  • collect_model_table() ✓
  • ReportConfig ✓
  • Unit conversion for output ✓

Why: Reporting queries solved variables by name; DC just has fewer to report.

3. What Needs to Be DC-Specific

3.1 New Trait (1 file)

File: src/foundation/formulation_traits.jl

"""
    DCPowerFlow <: FormulationTrait

DC power flow formulation with linearized equations.

# Variables
- Voltage angles only: θ (no voltage magnitudes)

# Residuals
- Active power balance only: P = 0 (no reactive power)

# Approximations
1. Voltage magnitudes ≈ 1.0 pu (flat voltage profile)
2. Line resistance negligible: r << x
3. Small angle differences: sin(θ) ≈ θ, cos(θ) ≈ 1
4. Branch flows: P_ij = (θ_i - θ_j) / x

# Characteristics
- Linear equations (direct solve, no iterations)
- Fast estimation for contingency analysis
- Good initial guess for AC power flow
- No voltage/reactive power information

# Use Cases
- Fast contingency screening (N-1, N-2 analysis)
- Initial estimate for AC Newton-Raphson
- Economic dispatch without voltage constraints
- Quick system study (topology changes, flow patterns)

# Limitations
- No voltage magnitudes → can't check voltage violations
- No reactive power → can't check Q limits, VAR support
- No transmission losses (r=0 assumption)
- Accuracy degrades for heavily loaded systems
"""
struct DCPowerFlow <: FormulationTrait end

export DCPowerFlow

3.2 Model Formulation Support (8 files)

Each model file adds DC-specific metadata:

Bus (src/models/bus/bus1ph.jl):

# DC variables: only angle (reference bus has θ=0 enforced by solver)
const BUS_VARS_DC = [
    ModelVar(:theta, AlgebVar(), Internal(); description="Voltage angle", units="rad")
]

# DC residuals: only P balance
const BUS_RESIDUALS_DC = [
    ModelResidual(:p, AlgebRes(), SharedRes(), :Bus, :p, :key; 
                  description="Active power balance")
]

function model_metadata(::Type{Bus})
    metadata = ModelMetadata(...)
    metadata.vars_by_formulation[DCPowerFlow] = BUS_VARS_DC
    metadata.residuals_by_formulation[DCPowerFlow] = BUS_RESIDUALS_DC
    return metadata
end

Powerful.supports_formulation(::Type{Bus}, ::Type{DCPowerFlow}) = true

Branch (src/models/branch.jl):

# DC variables: angles at both ends
const BRANCH_VARS_DC = [
    ModelVar(:theta_i, AlgebVar(), :Bus, :theta, :i),
    ModelVar(:theta_j, AlgebVar(), :Bus, :theta, :j),
]

# DC residuals: P contributions at both ends (no Q)
const BRANCH_RESIDUALS_DC = [
    ModelResidual(:p_i, AlgebRes(), SharedRes(), :Bus, :p, :i),
    ModelResidual(:p_j, AlgebRes(), SharedRes(), :Bus, :p, :j),
]

function model_metadata(::Type{Branch})
    metadata = ModelMetadata(...)
    metadata.vars_by_formulation[DCPowerFlow] = BRANCH_VARS_DC
    metadata.residuals_by_formulation[DCPowerFlow] = BRANCH_RESIDUALS_DC
    return metadata
end

# DC kernel (linear!)
@inline function dc_branch_kernel!(
    p_i_out, p_j_out, theta_i, theta_j, x, active, ::Type{<:Vector}
)
    @inbounds @simd for i in eachindex(p_i_out)
        mask = active[i]
        angle_diff = theta_i[i] - theta_j[i]
        p_flow = angle_diff / x[i]  # Linear: P = θ/x
        p_i_out[i] = mask * p_flow
        p_j_out[i] = mask * (-p_flow)
    end
    nothing
end

function calc_residuals!(ws::ResidualBuffers, model::BranchVec, ext::NamedTuple, ::DCPowerFlow)
    dc_branch_kernel!(ws.res_vals.p_i, ws.res_vals.p_j,
                      ws.var_vals.theta_i, ws.var_vals.theta_j,
                      model.x, ws.active_mask, typeof(model.x))
end

Powerful.supports_formulation(::Type{Branch}, ::Type{DCPowerFlow}) = true

PQ Load (src/models/pq.jl):

const PQ_VARS_DC = [
    ModelVar(:theta, AlgebVar(), :Bus, :theta, :i)
]

const PQ_RESIDUALS_DC = [
    ModelResidual(:p, AlgebRes(), SharedRes(), :Bus, :p, :i)
]

function model_metadata(::Type{PQ})
    metadata = ModelMetadata(...)
    metadata.vars_by_formulation[DCPowerFlow] = PQ_VARS_DC
    metadata.residuals_by_formulation[DCPowerFlow] = PQ_RESIDUALS_DC
    return metadata
end

# DC kernel (constant P, ignore ZIP model since V=1.0)
@inline function dc_pq_kernel!(p_out, pl, active, ::Type{<:Vector})
    @inbounds @simd for i in eachindex(p_out)
        mask = active[i]
        p_out[i] = mask * pl[i]  # Withdrawal (positive)
    end
    nothing
end

function calc_residuals!(ws::ResidualBuffers, model::PQVec, ext::NamedTuple, ::DCPowerFlow)
    dc_pq_kernel!(ws.res_vals.p, model.pl, ws.active_mask, typeof(model.pl))
end

Powerful.supports_formulation(::Type{PQ}, ::Type{DCPowerFlow}) = true

PV Generator (src/models/pv.jl):

# DC: PV acts like PQ (specified P, ignore voltage control)
const PV_VARS_DC = [
    ModelVar(:theta, AlgebVar(), :Bus, :theta, :i)
]

const PV_RESIDUALS_DC = [
    ModelResidual(:p, AlgebRes(), SharedRes(), :Bus, :p, :i)
]

function model_metadata(::Type{PV})
    metadata = ModelMetadata(...)
    metadata.vars_by_formulation[DCPowerFlow] = PV_VARS_DC
    metadata.residuals_by_formulation[DCPowerFlow] = PV_RESIDUALS_DC
    return metadata
end

# DC kernel (constant P injection, negative for generation)
@inline function dc_pv_kernel!(p_out, pg, active, ::Type{<:Vector})
    @inbounds @simd for i in eachindex(p_out)
        mask = active[i]
        p_out[i] = mask * (-pg[i])  # Injection (negative)
    end
    nothing
end

function calc_residuals!(ws::ResidualBuffers, model::PVVec, ext::NamedTuple, ::DCPowerFlow)
    dc_pv_kernel!(ws.res_vals.p, model.pg, ws.active_mask, typeof(model.pg))
end

Powerful.supports_formulation(::Type{PV}, ::Type{DCPowerFlow}) = true

Shunt (src/models/shunt.jl):

# DC: Shunts have no effect (Q devices, ignored in DC)
Powerful.supports_formulation(::Type{Shunt}, ::Type{DCPowerFlow}) = true

function model_metadata(::Type{Shunt})
    metadata = ModelMetadata(...)
    # No variables or residuals in DC (passive in P)
    metadata.vars_by_formulation[DCPowerFlow] = []
    metadata.residuals_by_formulation[DCPowerFlow] = []
    return metadata
end

Transformer (src/models/transformer.jl):

# DC: Similar to Branch but with tap ratio consideration
const TRANSFORMER_VARS_DC = [
    ModelVar(:theta_i, AlgebVar(), :Bus, :theta, :i),
    ModelVar(:theta_j, AlgebVar(), :Bus, :theta, :j),
]

const TRANSFORMER_RESIDUALS_DC = [
    ModelResidual(:p_i, AlgebRes(), SharedRes(), :Bus, :p, :i),
    ModelResidual(:p_j, AlgebRes(), SharedRes(), :Bus, :p, :j),
]

function model_metadata(::Type{Transformer})
    metadata = ModelMetadata(...)
    metadata.vars_by_formulation[DCPowerFlow] = TRANSFORMER_VARS_DC
    metadata.residuals_by_formulation[DCPowerFlow] = TRANSFORMER_RESIDUALS_DC
    return metadata
end

# DC kernel (include tap ratio effect on angle difference)
@inline function dc_transformer_kernel!(
    p_i_out, p_j_out, theta_i, theta_j, x, tap, active, ::Type{<:Vector}
)
    @inbounds @simd for i in eachindex(p_i_out)
        mask = active[i]
        # Simplified: P = (theta_i - theta_j) / (x * tap^2)
        angle_diff = theta_i[i] - theta_j[i]
        admittance = 1.0 / (x[i] * tap[i]^2)
        p_flow = angle_diff * admittance
        p_i_out[i] = mask * p_flow
        p_j_out[i] = mask * (-p_flow)
    end
    nothing
end

Powerful.supports_formulation(::Type{Transformer}, ::Type{DCPowerFlow}) = true

3.3 Solver Path (Modify existing)

Option A: Newton solver (works but inefficient)

Current solve_powerflow_newton() works unchanged! DC is just Newton with:

  • 1 iteration (linear problem)
  • Sparse Jacobian (constant B' matrix)

Option B: Direct linear solve (recommended)

Add fast path for linear formulations:

File: src/solvers/powerflow.jl (or new dc_powerflow.jl)

"""
    solve_dc_powerflow(sys::SystemModel; kwargs...) -> PowerFlowSolution

Direct linear solve for DC power flow.

Much faster than Newton for DC since problem is linear: B'θ = P_net
"""
function solve_dc_powerflow(sys::SystemModel; verbose::Bool=false)
    prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, DCPowerFlow())
    am = prob.address_manager
    
    # Build B' matrix (constant, sparse)
    B_prime = build_dc_admittance_matrix(am, sys)
    
    # Build P_net vector (sum of all injections)
    P_net = build_dc_injection_vector(am, sys)
    
    # Solve B'θ = P_net (direct, no iterations)
    theta = B_prime \ P_net
    
    # Package solution
    y = zeros(am.next_var - 1)
    copy_angles_to_dae!(y, theta, am, sys)
    
    return PowerFlowSolution(
        true, y, 0.0, 1,  # converged=true, residual=0, iterations=1
        :Success, nothing, prob
    )
end

function build_dc_admittance_matrix(am::AddressManager, sys::SystemModel)
    # Sparse matrix construction from branch data
    # B'[i,j] = -1/x_ij for branches
    # B'[i,i] = sum of connected branch susceptances
    # (Similar to Y-bus construction but simpler)
    ...
end

Integration with solve() API:

# In power_flow_api.jl _solve() dispatch
function _solve(
    prob::ACPowerFlowProblem{DCPowerFlow},
    alg::AlgorithmConfig{<:NewtonRaphsonMethod, NoGlobalization, NativeBackend};
    kwargs...
)
    # Fast path: DC is linear, skip Newton iterations
    return solve_dc_powerflow(prob.sys; kwargs...)
end

3.4 Reference Bus Handling

DC requires one angle reference (θ_slack = 0):

Option 1: Implicit (eliminate from system)

# In setup_with_formulation! for DCPowerFlow:
# - Don't allocate address for slack bus angle
# - Adjust branch equations to assume θ_slack = 0

Option 2: Explicit (add constraint)

# Add residual: theta_slack = 0
# Let linear solver handle the constraint

Recommend Option 1 (matches power flow convention).

5. Code Examples: User Perspective

5.1 Basic DC Power Flow

using Powerful, PowerFlowData

# Parse case
case = parse_network("cases/ieee14.raw")
sys = SystemModel(case)

# Solve DC power flow (linear, fast)
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, DCPowerFlow())
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson())  # Converges in 1 iteration

# Access results
θ = get_var(sol, :Bus, :theta, 1)  # Angle at bus 1
p_flow = get_var(sol, :Branch, :p_i, (1, 2, "1"))  # Power flow

# Report results
bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus)
# Only shows: bus_id, theta, p_net (no voltage, no Q)

5.2 Compare AC vs DC

# AC power flow (nonlinear, slow, accurate)
prob_ac = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, PowerInjection())
sol_ac = solve(prob_ac, NewtonRaphson())

# DC power flow (linear, fast, approximate)
prob_dc = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, DCPowerFlow())
sol_dc = solve(prob_dc, NewtonRaphson())

# Compare results
for bus_id in bus_ids
    θ_ac = get_var(sol_ac, :Bus, :theta, bus_id)
    θ_dc = get_var(sol_dc, :Bus, :theta, bus_id)
    println("Bus $bus_id: AC=$θ_ac, DC=$θ_dc, error=$(abs(θ_ac - θ_dc))")
end

5.3 DC as Initial Guess for AC

# Fast DC solve for initial estimate
prob_dc = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, DCPowerFlow())
sol_dc = solve(prob_dc, NewtonRaphson())

# Extract angles, assume V=1.0
y0_ac = zeros(2 * n_buses)  # [θ..., V...]
y0_ac[1:n_buses] .= sol_dc.y  # Angles from DC
y0_ac[n_buses+1:end] .= 1.0   # Flat voltage profile

# AC solve with warm start
prob_ac = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, PowerInjection(); initial_guess=y0_ac)
sol_ac = solve(prob_ac, NewtonRaphson())
# Likely converges faster than flat start

5.4 Formulation API Consistency

# Same API for all three formulations
formulations = [PowerInjection(), CurrentInjection(), DCPowerFlow()]

for form in formulations
    prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, form)
    sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson())
    println("$(typeof(form)): converged=$(sol.converged), iters=$(sol.iterations)")
end

7. Testing Strategy

7.1 Correctness Tests

@testitem "DC Power Flow Correctness" begin
    using Powerful, PowerFlowData
    
    case = parse_network("cases/ieee14.raw")
    sys = SystemModel(case)
    
    # Test 1: DC solves successfully
    prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, DCPowerFlow())
    sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson())
    @test sol.converged
    @test sol.iterations == 1  # Linear, converges in 1 iteration
    
    # Test 2: Power balance satisfied
    # Sum of all P injections should be zero (neglecting losses)
    p_net = sum(get_all_vars(sol, :Bus, :p))
    @test abs(p_net) < 1e-10
    
    # Test 3: Reference bus angle is zero
    θ_slack = get_var(sol, :Bus, :theta, slack_bus_id)
    @test abs(θ_slack) < 1e-12
    
    # Test 4: Kirchhoff's current law at each bus
    for bus_id in bus_ids
        p_injected = get_var(sol, :Bus, :p, bus_id)
        @test abs(p_injected) < 1e-8
    end
end

7.2 Consistency Tests

@testitem "DC vs AC Consistency" begin
    # DC should approximate AC when:
    # 1. Voltages are near 1.0 pu
    # 2. Angle differences are small (<15°)
    # 3. Resistance is small (r << x)
    
    case = parse_network("cases/ieee14.raw")  # Well-conditioned case
    sys = SystemModel(case)
    
    sol_ac = solve(ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, PowerInjection()), NewtonRaphson())
    sol_dc = solve(ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, DCPowerFlow()), NewtonRaphson())
    
    # Angles should be close (within a few percent)
    for bus_id in bus_ids
        θ_ac = get_var(sol_ac, :Bus, :theta, bus_id)
        θ_dc = get_var(sol_dc, :Bus, :theta, bus_id)
        @test abs(θ_ac - θ_dc) < 0.05  # Within 0.05 radians (≈3°)
    end
    
    # Power flows should be close (within 5-10%)
    for branch in branches
        p_ac = get_var(sol_ac, :Branch, :p_i, branch.key)
        p_dc = get_var(sol_dc, :Branch, :p_i, branch.key)
        @test abs(p_ac - p_dc) < 0.1 * abs(p_ac)  # Within 10%
    end
end

7.3 Performance Tests

@testitem "DC Performance" begin
    case = parse_network("cases/ACTIVSg2000.raw")
    sys = SystemModel(case)
    
    # DC should be much faster than AC
    t_dc = @elapsed solve(ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, DCPowerFlow()), NewtonRaphson())
    t_ac = @elapsed solve(ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, PowerInjection()), NewtonRaphson())
    
    @test t_dc < 0.1 * t_ac  # DC should be <10% of AC time
    println("Speedup: $(round(t_ac / t_dc, digits=1))x")
end

9. Alternative Considered: Separate Problem Type

Pros:

  • Clear separation of linear vs nonlinear solvers
  • Could optimize data structures for DC (e.g., no voltage arrays)
  • Simpler mental model for beginners ("DC is different")

Cons (outweigh pros):

  • Duplicates 90% of infrastructure (models, addressing, reporting)
  • API inconsistency (different problem construction, different solve call)
  • Maintenance burden (two code paths for similar functionality)
  • Lost opportunities (can't easily compare formulations)
  • Conflicts with existing architecture (formulations are for this!)

Verdict: Not recommended. Use FormulationTrait.

10. Conclusion

Summary

Recommended Architecture:

  1. Add DCPowerFlow <: FormulationTrait
  2. Extend model metadata with DC-specific vars/residuals
  3. Implement DC kernels (linear approximations)
  4. Add fast path: direct linear solve (optional, can use Newton initially)
  5. All infrastructure reused unchanged

Minimal Changes:

  • 1 new trait definition
  • 8 model files extended (add metadata + kernels)
  • 1 optional new solver (direct linear solve)
  • 0 changes to AddressManager, SystemModel, DAE, reporting, topology

Maximum Benefit:

  • Consistent API across all formulations
  • Easy comparison (AC vs DC accuracy/speed)
  • Natural extension for future formulations
  • Educational value (demonstrates linearization)

Should powerflow.jl be renamed?

Answer: No, but consider organizing solvers by method, not formulation.

Current structure is good:

  • powerflow.jl - Newton-Raphson implementation (works for all formulations)
  • power_flow_api.jl - Problem types and solve interface
  • dc_powerflow.jl (new) - Direct linear solver (DC-specific optimization)

Future could add:

  • fast_decoupled.jl - Fast Decoupled method (AC-specific)
  • gauss_seidel.jl - Iterative method (AC-specific)

Formulations live in foundation layer, solvers live in solver layer. Clean separation.

11. Open Questions

  1. Reference bus handling: Implicit elimination vs explicit constraint?

    • Recommend: Implicit (standard in power flow)

  2. DC transformer model: Include tap ratio effects?

    • Recommend: Yes, affects angle differences

  3. Distributed slack: Support multiple reference buses?

    • Recommend: Phase 2 feature (after basic DC works)

  4. DC optimal power flow: Linear programming integration?

    • Recommend: Separate feature, use DCPowerFlow as base

  5. Comparison metrics: Built-in AC/DC comparison tools?

    • Recommend: Yes, add compare_formulations(sys, [PowerInjection(), DCPowerFlow()])

Appendix A: Mathematical Background

DC Power Flow Approximations

Starting from AC power flow:

P_ij = V_i V_j (G_ij cos(θ_i - θ_j) + B_ij sin(θ_i - θ_j))

DC approximations:

  1. Flat voltage: Vi ≈ Vj ≈ 1.0 pu
  2. Resistive losses negligible: G_ij ≈ 0 (r << x)
  3. Small angles: sin(θi - θj) ≈ θi - θj, cos(θi - θj) ≈ 1

Result:

P_ij ≈ B_ij (θ_i - θ_j) = (θ_i - θ_j) / x_ij

Matrix form:

P = B' θ

Where B' is the DC admittance matrix (purely imaginary part of Y-bus).

When DC is Accurate

Good approximation when:

  • Voltage magnitudes: 0.95 < V < 1.05 pu
  • Angle differences: |θi - θj| < 15° (0.26 rad)
  • X/R ratio: x/r > 5
  • Loading: System not near voltage collapse

Typical accuracy:

  • Angles: Within 1-3° of AC solution
  • Power flows: Within 5-10% of AC solution
  • Losses: Not captured (r=0 assumption)

Limitations

Cannot model:

  • Voltage violations (no V variables)
  • Reactive power issues (no Q equations)
  • VAR support requirements
  • Voltage stability limits
  • Transmission losses
  • Voltage-dependent loads (ZIP model)
  • Voltage control actions

Use AC power flow when these matter.
